QuestionStmt.S: The sum to infinite terms of the series $$\tan^{-1} \left( \frac{1}{3} \right) + \tan^{-1} \left( \frac{2}{9} \right) + \ldots + \tan^{-1} \left( \frac{2^{n-1}}{1+2^{2n-1}} \right) + \ldots$$ is

Solution.S:
The general term of the series is $\tan^{-1} \left( \frac{2^{n-1}}{1+2^{2n-1}} \right)$.

We can rewrite it as:
$$\frac{2^{n-1}}{1+2^{2n-1}} = \frac{2^n - 2^{n-1}}{1 + 2^n \cdot 2^{n-1}}$$

Using the formula $\tan^{-1} a - \tan^{-1} b = \tan^{-1} \left( \frac{a-b}{1+ab} \right)$, we get:
$$\tan^{-1} \left( \frac{2^n - 2^{n-1}}{1 + 2^n \cdot 2^{n-1}} \right) = \tan^{-1} 2^n - \tan^{-1} 2^{n-1}$$

Thus the series telescopes:
$$S_n = (\tan^{-1} 2 - \tan^{-1} 1) + (\tan^{-1} 4 - \tan^{-1} 2) + \ldots + (\tan^{-1} 2^n - \tan^{-1} 2^{n-1})$$
$$= \tan^{-1} 2^n - \tan^{-1} 1 = \tan^{-1} 2^n - \frac{\pi}{4}$$

Taking the limit as $n \to \infty$:
$$S_\infty = \lim_{n\to\infty} \tan^{-1} 2^n - \frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{2} - \frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{4}$$

Hence the correct option is A: $\frac{\pi}{4}$.
